rv.q: In a re-defining performance, Rankin makes Muriel Spark’s extraordinary heroine more extraordinary still.
Atmospheric, visceral and cerebral, this is narrative theatre at its very best.
It’s quite simply a symposium of modern Scottish theatrical excellence, National Theatre of Scotland has outdone itself with this retelling of one of the most pivotal and most Edinburgh of stories...
And, in the National Theatre of Scotland’s new production, homecoming star Gayle Rankin captures all the character’s complexities in a thrillingly charismatic performance.

Vicky Featherstone’s beautifully paced production runs to three hours, unfolding with the force of a slow-motion eruption, and nicely choreographed to make use of the varying levels afforded by Chloe Lamford’s amphitheatre-style set design.

Rankin has all of the charisma needed to bring Brodie to life, so gripping in the play’s first act that the audience gets a taste of what it must have been like to be one of the girls in the “Brodie set”.
The production ultimately prioritises Brodie's bohemian charm over her danger, resulting in a revival that lacks its intended bite.
The play is amazing and I would totally recommend.
The National Theatre of Scotland’s new expressionistic production of ‘The Prime of Miss Jean Brodie’ is a magnificent theatrical gem.

This vibrant production (from the National Theatre of Scotland, The Royal Lyceum and Pitlochry Festival Theatre) breathes new life into the old favourite, amplifying the teacher's allure as well as her failings.
This is terrific narrative theatre, "atmospheric, visceral and cerebral".
Harrower, Featherstone and co's mighty rendering breathes vital life into a classic work to reinvent it anew.
Gayle Rankin makes the role her own and totally runs with it.
This story of a bold, outspoken, but dangerous schoolmistress has been rejuvenated, updated, and brought into sharp focus for the 21st century in this powerful new production.

The fine performances of this outstanding ensemble, together with Vickie Featherstone's fine staging of Harrower's adaptation, and Gayle's Rankin's truly mesmerizing Jean Brodie, were greeted by a long, enthusiastic applause.

Ferocious, visually astonishing, and intellectually rigorous, this co-production with Pitlochry Festival Theatre proves that the shadows of fascism can take root just as easily in the sunlit classrooms of Auld Reekie as they do upon the world stage – leaving an icy, haunting aftertaste that lingers.
To call Vicky Featherstone’s production spectacular is to understate the case...
Rankin embodies Brodie’s rejection of formality, in a vibrant rebellion.
I found myself immersed in the story and captivated by the characters and can recommend this The Prime of Miss Jean Brodie highly.
This is undoubtedly a serious and grown-up piece of theatre, staged with precision, skill and considerable verve.
It is a pity the production’s length and missteps with the set make for a play that cannot fully deliver on its potential.
Where the novel is a spark, this is a mere flicker.
The Prime of Miss Jean Brodie is one of those shows, the acting, costumes, and staging, everything is a masterpiece to behold.
This outstanding adaptation seems so faithful to Spark's novel and so relevant to our times.
This is a wonderful production that is hampered by a script that loses sight of the heart of the story.

This production is well acted and raises questions about how far-right politics get a foothold in a society. However, it wants to see Miss Brodie as a misunderstood woman of her time, rather than as Muriel Spark conceived her: a savage soul intent on replicating herself.

cn.t: Critics hail this National Theatre of Scotland production as a magnificent, monumental revival, with Gayle Rankin delivering a captivating, utterly compelling performance in the title role, though some find the adaptation leans too comfortably into charm.
